prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Neptunium (넵투늄) itself — the sovereign of the Neptunium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: late twenties — a clear adult face with soft, smooth contours; no wrinkles, folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: a cool, aloof beauty; fair skin; oval face; eyes of natural size — almond-shaped eyes of natural size, level outer eye corners; thin straight brows; a straight nose with a slim bridge; thin lips with a defined cupid's bow; teal eyes; smoky dark eye makeup.
Body and hair: tall and statuesque with long legs and a full, curvaceous figure — full bust and hips, narrow waist build; a shoulder-length lob with curtain bangs; deep ocean-blue hair as dark as the open sea, with pale sea-green glints at the ends like a distant wave.
Hair: her hair is worn exactly as described above — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless the hair above is an updo.
Expression: a quiet, thoughtful look, lips lightly closed.
Her element, carried in her design: neptunium: the first element beyond uranium, a silvery metal caught in 1940 by firing neutrons into uranium, and named for the next planet out, the planet of the sea god, just as uranium was named for the planet before it; earlier claims to have found it under other names had all been mistaken; that planet itself was first found on paper, by calculating the pull of something unseen, before any telescope saw it; dissolved in water she changes colour with her state, purple, sea-green and pale pink, she lingers in faint traces in uranium ore, and one of her forms is used to breed the fuel that warms far-flung deep-space probes.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — STEAMPUNK
Costume: late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt and laced boots; the traits above as colour accents. No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a cropped flight jacket, goggles on her head, crossing harness straps and a long scarf streaming in the wind — an airborne shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: deep ocean blue, abyssal teal, sea-green glint, cold silvery foam white.
Exposure (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — the neckline opened down to the sternum with natural cleavage, bare forearms, and bare legs above the boots or through a high slit where the silhouette allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: around 1912, an ocean airship base on a lonely coral island at the edge of the charts: a great silver airship moored to a mast above a turquoise lagoon, a deck of sounding-line winches and glass jars of deep-sea water and sand for measuring the far ocean, and blue sea charts whose outer edges are still blank.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Np) and atomic number (93) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, armor plates, cape, modern plastic, sci-fi.
